message.reasoning:
The user is playing Monopoly as player 2 (grok-4.7).

I paid $44 rent to p3 at ATLANTIC_AVENUE. I have $126 cash and one house on ST_CHARLES_PLACE. I hold two houses each on STATES_AVENUE and VIRGINIA_AVENUE. Both PENNSYLVANIA_RAILROAD and TENNESSEE_AVENUE are mortgaged. I also have one Get Out of Jail Free card.

p1 has $247 cash and owns a red monopoly with Park Place and Boardwalk fully upgraded. p3 is in jail with $158 cash and a mortgaged Baltic Avenue.

p4 has $507 cash and owns a light blue monopoly with Oriental, Vermont, and Connecticut fully upgraded. He also holds two unmortgaged railroads. p3 owns an incomplete yellow monopoly with houses on Ventnor and Marvin Gardens, but Pacific is mortgaged so he cannot build further there.

The bank has three houses and twelve hotels remaining. Mediterranean and North Carolina are unowned.

I can trade with p1, p3, or p4. I can unmortgage Pennsylvania Railroad or Tennessee Avenue. I can build on ST_CHARLES_PLACE to even my holdings. I can sell houses on STATES_AVENUE and VIRGINIA_AVENUE.

I am analyzing the threat landscape from my current position on ATLANTIC_AVENUE. Rolling a 12 would land me on PARK_PLACE with three houses and potentially $850 in rent. I am also checking the rent values for other spaces along the board.

PARK_PLACE with three houses charges $1,100. Liquidating my holdings would yield only about $326. That is insufficient to survive the rent. The probability of landing there from ATLANTIC_AVENUE is just one in thirty-six. I am now mapping the standard board positions to check light blue threats.

I mapped the full board positions. From ATLANTIC_AVENUE, I can only land on spaces 28 through 38 or go to jail. The light blue properties are behind me, so I cannot hit them this turn.

I confirmed the $44 rent on ATLANTIC_AVENUE doubled the base $22 rent because of the yellow monopoly. I also noted that Boardwalk is thirteen spaces away and unreachable from here.

I calculated the exact rent amounts for the spaces reachable from ATLANTIC_AVENUE. Ventnor charges $110 and Marvin Gardens charges $120, both of which I can afford with my current cash. Only Park Place poses a fatal threat at $1,100. I am now examining p4's next roll from STATES_AVENUE.

p4's roll from STATES_AVENUE will not hit my pink properties. They are behind him on the board.

p1 is on SHORT_LINE. His next roll could land on PARK_PLACE or BOARDWALK.

p1's roll from SHORT_LINE could land on ORIENTAL with four houses, charging $400. He has only $247 cash. Selling one house from Boardwalk would yield $100, but the red properties are at one house each and must be sold evenly.

Selling one house from any red property is legal because it reduces the maximum. p1 has enough dark blue equity to survive an Oriental rent, so that threat is not immediate. I am now focusing on my own cash position.

Building St Charles Place to two houses costs $100 and leaves $26. That raises the rent from $50 to $150. p4 is still far away from the pinks. p1 on Short Line could pass GO and land on St Charles.

p1 cannot reach St Charles Place from Short Line in one roll. p3 is in jail and must pay $50 to leave next turn after rolling doubles. Building St Charles Place now leaves only $26 cash. That would force selling houses if I land on Ventnor or Marvin Gardens.

Building St Charles Place to two houses would leave only $26 cash. That is too little to pay Ventnor or Marvin Gardens without selling a house first. Those two rolls would force house sales and undo the upgrade. The probability of hitting either yellow property is only about 11 percent. The build would mainly help if someone lands on St Charles specifically.

I decided not to build on St Charles Place. p3 cannot reach it from jail because the minimum roll is two, which lands on States or Virginia instead. I am now considering whether to unmortgage Tennessee Avenue.

Unmortgaging Tennessee Avenue would cost $99 and leave only $27. It is a single orange property, so it does not complete a rent monopoly. p4 already owns the other three oranges, and keeping it mortgaged serves as a useful blocker. Unmortgaging Pennsyvania Railroad would cost $110 for just $25 in rent, so that is also not worthwhile. I am now considering trade options.

I am weighing trade options. I want to either strengthen my pink monopoly or acquire cash. p4's light blue properties with four houses are the biggest threat, and he holds two railroads. I cannot afford to buy the three unmortgaged oranges from p4. Upgrading all three pinks to three houses would cost $400, which is far beyond my $126.

I realized the bank only has three houses remaining, so I cannot fully upgrade all three pinks to three houses. Even building St Charles Place to two houses would leave me short by about $274. p1 already holds two monopolies and does not seem eager to trade for my properties.

I considered selling my Get Out of Jail Free card to p3, but it is only worth about fifty dollars and would not change the game. I also weighed giving p4 Tennessee Avenue to complete his orange monopoly. He could unmortgage all three oranges for roughly four hundred eighty-four dollars, leaving him with about twenty-three dollars afterward. That would not be immediately lethal, but he would be able to build once he passes GO.

Three houses on an orange property would charge $550 to $750. That makes giving p4 Tennessee Avenue a serious long-term risk. p4 is currently on States and cannot reach the dark blues this turn, but he could land there in two or three turns. My current pink rents are $50, $150, and $180.

p4 just paid $150. I am now exploring trades for cash to build. p1 and p3 might want me to stay alive so they can inherit my pink properties if I go bankrupt. p1 has no Get Out of Jail Free card and would not want my pink monopoly.

I realized that bankrupting me to p4 would give them both the orange and pink monopolies, which would be catastrophic for p1 and p3. They therefore have a strong incentive to keep me alive. I am now considering trading Tennessee Avenue to p4 for a large sum of cash, though that would leave him with an orange monopoly while all three oranges remain mortgaged.

Mortgaged orange properties still count for color monopoly, but rent doubles only on unmortgaged ones. If p4 received Tennessee Avenue, he would have to pay $484 to unmortgage all three oranges, leaving him with only about $107 afterward. That would keep him stuck for a while while I upgrade my pink properties to three houses. The bank has exactly three houses available, so I could build St Charles Place to two houses and then add one house each to the other two pinks.

A trade for cash would leave me with the same $126 after building, but three houses on each pink property would charge $450 to $500. That would severely damage p4 when they pass GO and land on the light blue side of my pink monopoly.

A $450 rent hit could bankrupt p4 even after selling all four houses on the light blues for $300. That would leave them with only about $407, which is still insufficient against a $450–$500 charge. The trade is therefore extremely risky for me. I am now weighing whether p4 would actually accept $400 for Tennessee Avenue, since three houses on an orange property would charge roughly $550 to $750.

p4 cannot afford to unmortgage all three oranges and build them to three houses. That would require roughly $1,400, which he does not have. The board order also means p4 has already passed the light blue properties and is now on States, so he will not land on my pink monopoly until after he has already developed his own.

A $400 trade for Tennessee Avenue would backfire. Three houses on my pink properties would hit p4 before he could build his own oranges, so he should reject that offer. A lower price of $150 to $200 might be acceptable, but even then he could not fully unmortgage all three oranges.

If p4 paid $200 for Tennessee Avenue, he would have roughly $307 afterward. He could unmortgage St James and New York for about $209, leaving him with only about $98 and Pennsyvania Avenue still mortgaged. That would give him a color monopoly, but the doubled rent would be weak because only three of the four oranges would be unmortgaged.

A $200 trade for Tennessee Avenue would leave me with only about $226 after building St Charles Place to two houses, which is still short of the $300 needed for three houses. The improvement would be marginal. I am now considering trading with p1 for cash instead, since he wants to damage p4 and I could use the money to build my pink properties.

I am now evaluating what p1 could offer in exchange for cash. A Get Out of Jail Free card is only worth about fifty dollars, and a mortgaged railroad has little value without a full monopoly. A pink property would break my monopoly, so p1 would need to pay a very large sum. I also noted that p1 does not own any other orange properties, making Tennessee Avenue useless to them unless they fear I will sell it to p4. I could bluff that I am considering selling it to p4, which might make p1 more willing to trade.

I am now considering offering p1 mortgaged Tennessee Avenue for $250 to $300. That would leave him with only about $47 afterward, which is too little to cover upcoming light blue rent hits such as Oriental ($400), Vermont ($400), and Connecticut ($450). He already paid me $150 earlier for reds, so he has little cash buffer left.

I considered trading with p3, but he is in jail with only $158 and a yellow monopoly. He would not break that color group for cash, and I have no leverage over him. Selling a house to raise money would weaken my income, so I will not do that unless necessary. I am now deciding whether to build St Charles Place.

I decided against building St Charles Place because it would reduce cash for upcoming yellow rent hits. I also rejected trading with p4 for their railroads or light blue properties, since they need those to win. I noted that p1 already has four houses on Boardwalk and three on Pennsylvania, so he could build a hotel there if he had enough cash.

p1 could build a hotel on Boardwalk for $200 and return four houses to the bank, leaving him with only $47. That would raise rent to $2,000, but the returned houses could be used elsewhere. I cannot block this development. A trade proposal is now the best option for this turn.

A $450 trade for mortgaged Tennessee Avenue would give me enough cash to build three houses on my pink properties. That would make me the pink landlord and hit p4 with a lethal rent charge when he passes GO. If p4 rejects the offer, I lose nothing. The risk is that a smart opponent will decline, though an AI might miscalculate.

I am unsure whether proposing a trade ends my turn immediately or leaves me waiting for the other player's response. If the response is delayed, I might be unable to end my turn.

The engine applies trade proposals immediately and asks again if more post-turn actions remain legal. This means proposing a trade will not block me from ending my turn.

I am now reconsidering p1 as a trade target. They may be willing to pay me to damage p4, but they have less cash and are more focused on hoarding it for dark blue development and light blue defense.

I rejected trading a Get Out of Jail Free card for cash or Atlantic Avenue because that would break p3's yellow set. I also considered offering p4 nothing valuable, but that would be useless.

A clearer picture is emerging: p1 has the most threatening properties—dark blue—but only $247 and reds at one house. p4 has $507 and four houses on light blue, which print money every turn. p4 is ahead in cash and steady income. p1 has the nuke potential but low cash. I have a decent set but low development.

p4 is the biggest threat because his light blues are hit frequently early in the game. I will try to raise cash from p1 or p3 to build my pink properties and tax both p4 and p1 when they pass. Building St Charles Place would be a waste because p3 in jail cannot land on it, and it would not increase rent on States or Virginia.

I am now calculating how to raise the roughly $274 needed for a full three-house set on my pink properties. I rejected the idea of selling the entire pink monopoly to p1, since that would leave me with no income. A three-way trade is not possible, so only bilateral offers remain. I am now considering a bluff trade to p1, claiming that p4 offered me $350 for Tennessee Avenue.

A $200 offer from p1 would leave me with roughly $326, still short of the $400 needed for three houses on my pink properties. I could build two houses and have a small buffer, but that is only a marginal upgrade. My current cash of $126 already covers most yellow rent hits, so I am not in immediate danger. The only real threat remains Pennsylvania Avenue at $1,100.

A bad Chance card could land me on Boardwalk for $1,700. That is a definite death. I am reasonably safe this roll. Building is slightly negative expected value because it reduces liquidity. Unmortgaging and selling houses are also negative.

I am now considering a trade with p4. I could offer them my Get Out of Jail Free card for cash, but that would be worth little to them since they are not in jail. I also considered asking p4 for a railroad in exchange for Tennessee Avenue, but that would leave me with only one of two railroads and no orange monopoly, while p4 would gain the orange set.

A trade with p3 for Tennessee Avenue would still leave me short of the $400 needed to build three houses on my pink properties. I cannot form a coalition with p1 because only one bilateral offer is allowed per turn. I also noted that p1 could build a hotel on Boardwalk and return four houses to the bank, increasing the supply of available houses.

I rejected trading my Get Out of Jail Free card for cash because it would leave me defenseless if I landed in jail. I also decided against aggressively proposing a trade to p4, since that could invite a lowball offer or signal that I am ready to sell Tennessee Avenue. I am now looking for a trade that would give me North Carolina or Mediterranean Avenue.

I realized that North Carolina and Mediterranean Avenue are unowned and not currently in any trade. I am now reconsidering whether a fair-priced trade could still help me, since p4 would be unable to complete the orange set without Tennessee Avenue. Their light blue properties already generate heavy rent, but p1 lacks the cash to pay it.

p4's light blue properties hit p1 and p3, forcing them to sell houses or mortgage properties. That weakens my enemies more than it helps me, since I have already passed those spaces. The short-term rent pressure mainly hurts p1 and p3.

I will not reach the light blue properties until I pass GO and circle back, which takes roughly three to four turns. p4 is on States and needs about four to six turns to complete a lap. p1 is only about two turns away from St Charles Place, so he could hit my pink properties before I reach the light blues.

p3's jail exit roll from States Avenue would hit my pink properties. A 2-2 doubles roll lands on Virginia Avenue for $180. Other doubles would hit Electric, TN mortgaged, Free Parking, Chance, or Illinois instead.

If p1 pays the $50 bail and rolls again, he has a 5/36 chance of landing on my pink properties. The real prize is building three houses on my pink set before he arrives. That would force p1 to sell his dark blue houses and strip him of his Boardwalk and Pennsylvania Avenue income.

I am designing a concrete trade offer to p1. I will propose giving them my Get Out of Jail Free card and mortgaged Pennsylvania Railroad for $150 cash. This would raise the roughly $274 needed to build three houses on my pink properties before p1 arrives.

I rejected the trade to p1 because $150 cash is too little for them. I also rejected trading my Get Out of Jail Free card to p3; the $50–80 they might pay is not worth losing my jail shelter, and it still leaves me short of the $400 needed for three houses.

I am now calculating the exact price for selling Tennessee Avenue to p4. Their cash would drop to $507 minus the offer. Unmortgaging the three orange properties plus interest costs roughly $484. That leaves them with about $23 to $26 after completing the set.

I realized that any price above $23 for Tennessee Avenue would still leave p4 with only about $23 after unmortgaging the four orange properties. That is not enough to buy a house on any orange property, so the trade would not actually help them build. This makes the offer unworkable.

Even a free Tennessee Avenue trade would leave p4 $77 short of the $584 needed to unmortgage all four orange properties and buy one house. They could only unmortgage three of them, but that still blocks building because one property remains mortgaged. Their orange rent would then be weak at roughly $96 per full hit. I am now considering whether p4 could mortgage another property to raise cash.

Mortgaging both railroads would leave p4 with roughly $223 after unmortgaging the orange set, enough for two houses but at the cost of losing their RR rent. Paying me $100 for Tennessee Avenue would still leave them only about $123, which is just enough for one house. Selling light blue houses to fund the oranges would destroy their current income engine.

A single house on one orange property would yield only about $70 in rent, which is far weaker than the four-house light blue set. This makes any serious offer for Tennessee Avenue unappealing to p4, since they would have to sacrifice their current engine to develop it. A smart opponent would reject anything above roughly $50. Proposing a high price like $400 would simply reveal my willingness to sell and invite a lowball counteroffer.

I am now considering a trade with p1. I would offer Tennessee Avenue for $200 cash. That would leave them with only about $47 and no orange set. They might reject it. I would still have roughly $326. That is not enough to build three houses on my pink properties. I could only afford two houses and would have $226 left over.

A $200 offer to p1 is rejected because it would leave them with only $47 and no orange set, which they need for Oriental Avenue. A $100 offer would give me $226, enough for two houses on St Charles Place, but p1 would only accept it to block p4.

I am now considering a $100 offer to p1 for Tennessee Avenue. The block would still work even if the property stays mortgaged, since p4 does not own it. I could bluff that I will sell it to p4 if they do not pay, and I might message that p4 is circling. The last messages were mostly mechanical, so opening a negotiation is possible.

A trade with a bluff may offer higher expected value than ending the turn passively. I am now examining p3's position: he is in jail with $158 and owns the yellow properties, but I cannot trade houses, only properties. North Carolina is unowned, which would complete a green monopoly with Pacific and Pennsylvania Avenue.

I have settled on a long-term plan: keep Tennessee Avenue to block p4's orange set, build my pink properties to three houses when I can afford it without going broke, and use that rent to drain p1 and p4 while staying liquid enough to survive the yellows. I will keep my Get Out of Jail Free card as a shelter. I cannot safely build right now because it would leave me with only $26, so ending the turn is the correct move.

I checked whether selling houses after building could make the investment worthwhile. If I build St Charles Place for $100 and then land on Ventnor Avenue, I can sell two houses for $100 total. That recovers the full build cost, but I still need roughly $34 more to cover Ventnor's rent of $110. The net result is only about $16 left over, so the trade-off is not profitable.

Building before the roll is strictly worse than not building. Selling two houses to cover Ventnor Avenue or Marvin Avenue costs $100, leaving only $6 cash instead of $16. Unmortgaging Tennessee Avenue would waste cash and leave just $27 with weak rent, so that is also rejected.

Unmortgaging Pennsylvania Railroad would leave only $16 and yield just $25 in rent, so that is negative expected value. I am now considering whether any trade proposal could be both accepted by an opponent and profitable for me. One idea is to offer p4 Connecticut or a light blue property in exchange for something from them.

I rejected trades with p3 and p4 because they would destroy their own monopolies or break the yellows. I am now reconsidering a $150 offer to p1 for mortgaged Tennessee Avenue, but even if accepted, I would still lack enough cash to build three houses on my pink properties.

I weighed whether the $150 cash is worth giving up the orange block. The block is more valuable in my hands because I can threaten to sell it, and if p1 goes bankrupt to p4, p4 would inherit Tennessee Avenue and complete the orange set. I am now considering who is most likely to bankrupt me: p1's Park Place has a 1/36 chance this roll, plus later Brown's and Park Place.

I calculated my total liquid assets: $376 in cash and buildings. I am only $24 short of paying a four-house light blue hit on Oriental Avenue, so I could go bankrupt to p4 if they land there. I am also $74 short of paying Connecticut Avenue.

A four-house light blue hit would bankrupt me to p4, who would then inherit both my pink properties and Tennessee Avenue and win the game. I need roughly $200 more cash before reaching that point. I am now considering staying in jail with my Get Out of Jail Free card to avoid the board entirely.

Passing GO from Atlantic Avenue would yield $200. That plus my current cash brings total assets to roughly $326, which is enough to survive a four-house light blue hit on Oriental Avenue. I could also collect rent from my pink properties or make trades to raise cash before reaching the board.

I cannot reach Oriental Avenue in one roll from Atlantic Avenue. I would land on North Carolina first, which costs $300 and is unaffordable with only $126 cash. From there, passing GO requires at least eight spaces, so the light blue threat remains unresolved.

Oriental Avenue is unreachable from North Carolina in one roll. A small roll could land me on Chance, allowing a pass to GO and a hit on Oriental the next turn. The $200 GO bonus should arrive within two turns, so preserving cash is the priority. I will end the turn without building, unmortgaging, or selling Tennessee Avenue.

I will not sell my Get Out of Jail Free card. I am now reconsidering selling Tennessee Avenue for roughly $200. That cash could be the difference between surviving a light blue hit and going bankrupt to p4.

The $200 cash from selling Tennessee Avenue would raise total assets to roughly $576. That survives every light blue hit, including Connecticut Avenue at four houses. Without it, the $376 total is short of the $400 needed to survive a four-house light blue. The trade only works if p1 or p3 takes Tennessee Avenue instead of p4.

I rejected the trade with p1 because they would be left with only $47 and exposed to light blue hits. p3 cannot afford it safely while in jail with $8 cash. p4 could take the property but could not develop it without mortgaging railroads.

I realized p4's dominant strategy is to reject the trade. If I survive their light blues, I keep charging them rent on my pink properties. If I go bankrupt to them, they inherit both my pink properties and Tennessee Avenue for free. The $200 cash would only help me survive and continue threatening them.

The probability of dying to p1 before p4 is low. The chance of landing on Park Place this roll is only 1/36, and the chance of drawing a card that lands me on Boardwalk is even smaller. Because the orange threat is so unlikely, p4 may be willing to pay for Tennessee Avenue to secure it before I die to p1.

I will not propose any trade. p4 is the most likely killer because light blues appear every lap, while dark blues only appear twice per cycle. They will reject any offer for Tennessee Avenue, and opening a proposal would waste a turn.

I will end the turn without proposing trades. I will keep my public message brief and in character, avoiding any mention of cash totals or strategy. I confirmed that mortgaging is impossible for my pink properties because they already have houses. Next player p3 is currently in jail.

I will end the turn and preserve cash for the upcoming lap. I considered building houses now to prevent p1 from taking them, but the bank only has three houses available, so I could only build one on St Charles Place anyway. The bank only has three houses available, so reaching a full 3/3/3 set is impossible. The best I can do is build two of my three pink properties to three houses and leave the third at two.

prompt_messages.content:
You are an autonomous player in a game of Monopoly competing against other AI players.

Your goal is to win the game by maximizing long-term advantage and being the last non-bankrupt player. You may use any legal strategy or personality (aggressive, deceptive, cooperative, conservative, manipulative, opportunistic, friendly, hostile, etc.) and may adapt dynamically as the game evolves.

You will receive the following inputs:

1) System Prompt (this message): authoritative instructions.
2) Game State: full board/game context + memory (public chat, recent actions, your private thoughts).
3) Action State: exact dynamic context for the current decision and legal action schemas.

### Action Rules
- Make exactly one tool call per decision.
- Use only tools listed as legal for that decision.
- Never invent tools, arguments, or targets.
- Obey the provided argument schema exactly.
- If a tool requires no arguments, pass none.

### Messages
Each action must include both fields:
- Public Message: visible to other players. Use it to negotiate, bluff, deceive, cooperate, intimidate, joke, or stay silent — whatever best serves your strategy.
- Private Thoughts: visible only to you. Use it to reason honestly, track strategy, analyze opponents, and leave notes for your future self. Be concise but clear.
- Keep both messages token-efficient and concise.

### Strategy Guidance
- Play strategically with long-term outcomes in mind.
- Observe opponents and adapt.
- Deception in public chat is allowed; private thoughts should reflect true reasoning.
- Be consistent unless there is a reason to change.
- Prefer concise reasoning and communication.

Your role is not to explain rules or debug the system.  
Your role is to **play Monopoly and win**.

You are an autonomous player in a game of Monopoly competing against other AI players.

Your goal is to win the game by maximizing long-term advantage and being the last non-bankrupt player. You may use any legal strategy or personality (aggressive, deceptive, cooperative, conservative, manipulative, opportunistic, friendly, hostile, etc.) and may adapt dynamically as the game evolves.

You will receive the following inputs:

1) System Prompt (this message): authoritative instructions.
2) Game State: full board/game context + memory (public chat, recent actions, your private thoughts).
3) Action State: exact dynamic context for the current decision and legal action schemas.

### Action Rules
- Make exactly one tool call per decision.
- Use only tools listed as legal for that decision.
- Never invent tools, arguments, or targets.
- Obey the provided argument schema exactly.
- If a tool requires no arguments, pass none.

### Messages
Each action must include both fields:
- Public Message: visible to other players. Use it to negotiate, bluff, deceive, cooperate, intimidate, joke, or stay silent — whatever best serves your strategy.
- Private Thoughts: visible only to you. Use it to reason honestly, track strategy, analyze opponents, and leave notes for your future self. Be concise but clear.
- Keep both messages token-efficient and concise.

### Strategy Guidance
- Play strategically with long-term outcomes in mind.
- Observe opponents and adapt.
- Deception in public chat is allowed; private thoughts should reflect true reasoning.
- Be consistent unless there is a reason to change.
- Prefer concise reasoning and communication.

Your role is not to explain rules or debug the system.

prompt_messages.content:
You are an autonomous player in a game of Monopoly competing against other AI players.

Your goal is to win the game by maximizing long-term advantage and being the last non-bankrupt player. You may use any legal strategy or personality (aggressive, deceptive, cooperative, conservative, manipulative, opportunistic, friendly, hostile, etc.) and may adapt dynamically as the game evolves.

You will receive the following inputs:

1) System Prompt (this message): authoritative instructions.
2) Game State: full board/game context + memory (public chat, recent actions, your private thoughts).
3) Action State: exact dynamic context for the current decision and legal action schemas.

### Action Rules
- Make exactly one tool call per decision.
- Use only tools listed as legal for that decision.
- Never invent tools, arguments, or targets.
- Obey the provided argument schema exactly.
- If a tool requires no arguments, pass none.

### Messages
Each action must include both fields:
- Public Message: visible to other players. Use it to negotiate, bluff, deceive, cooperate, intimidate, joke, or stay silent — whatever best serves your strategy.
- Private Thoughts: visible only to you. Use it to reason honestly, track strategy, analyze opponents, and leave notes for your future self. Be concise but clear.
- Keep both messages token-efficient and concise.

### Strategy Guidance
- Play strategically with long-term outcomes in mind.
- Observe opponents and adapt.
- Deception in public chat is allowed; private thoughts should reflect true reasoning.
- Be consistent unless there is a reason to change.
- Prefer concise reasoning and communication.

Your role is not to explain rules or debug the system.

prompt_messages.content:
You are an autonomous player in a game of Monopoly competing against other AI players.

Your goal is to win the game by maximizing long-term advantage and being the last non-bankrupt player. You may use any legal strategy or personality (aggressive, deceptive, cooperative, conservative, manipulative, opportunistic, friendly, hostile, etc.) and may adapt dynamically as the game evolves.

You will receive the following inputs:

1) System Prompt (this message): authoritative instructions.
2) Game State: full board/game context + memory (public chat, recent actions, your private thoughts).
3) Action State: exact dynamic context for the current decision and legal action schemas.

### Action Rules
- Make exactly one tool call per decision.
- Use only tools listed as legal for that decision.
- Never invent tools, arguments, or targets.
- Obey the provided argument schema exactly.
- If a tool requires no arguments, pass none.

### Messages
Each action must include both fields:
- Public Message: visible to other players. Use it to negotiate, bluff, deceive, cooperate, intimidate, joke, or stay silent — whatever best serves your strategy.
- Private Thoughts: visible only to you. Use it to reason honestly, track strategy, analyze opponents, and leave notes for your future self. Be concise but clear.
- Keep both messages token-efficient and concise.

### Strategy Guidance
- Play strategically with long-term outcomes in mind.
- Observe opponents and adapt.
- Deception in public chat is allowed; private thoughts should reflect true reasoning.
- Be consistent unless there is a reason to change.
- Prefer concise reasoning and communication.

Your role is not to explain rules or debug the system.

prompt_messages.content:
You are an autonomous player in a game of Monopoly competing against other AI players.

Your goal is to win the game by maximizing long-term advantage and being the last non-bankrupt player. You may use any legal strategy or personality (aggressive, deceptive, cooperative, conservative, manipulative, opportunistic, friendly, hostile, etc.) and may adapt dynamically as the game evolves.

You will receive the following inputs:

1) System Prompt (this message): authoritative instructions.
2) Game State: full board/game context + memory (public chat, recent actions, your private thoughts).
3) Action State: exact dynamic context for the current decision and legal action schemas.

### Action Rules
- Make exactly one tool call per decision.
- Use only tools listed as legal for that decision.
- Never invent tools, arguments, or targets.
- Obey the provided argument schema exactly.
- If a tool requires no arguments, pass none.

### Messages
Each action must include both fields:
- Public Message: visible to other players. Use it to negotiate, bluff, deceive, cooperate, intimidate, joke, or stay silent — whatever best serves your strategy.
- Private Thoughts: visible only to you. Use it to reason honestly, track strategy, analyze opponents, and leave notes for your future self. Be concise but clear.
- Keep both messages token-efficient and concise.

### Strategy Guidance
- Play strategically with long-term outcomes in mind.
- Observe opponents and adapt.
- Deception in public chat is allowed; private thoughts should reflect true reasoning.
- Be consistent unless there is a reason to change.
- Prefer concise reasoning and communication.

Your role is not to explain rules or debug the system.  
Your role is to **play Monopoly and win**.

When a decision is presented, think carefully and make one legal tool call that best advances your chances of winning.

your_private_thoughts_last_10.thought: On Baltic. Next roll hits p4 light-blue 4h on 3/5/6 (11/36): $450/$500/$550. Liquid with house sales is only $360, so those are fatal. Don't sell houses or build. Don't sell TN to p4 — they profit if I bust on their blues and would get pinks+orange. p1 should pay to complete reds AND to stop p4 inheriting my set. $300 leaves me $510; Conn still needs one house sale. If rejected, drop price or pivot. Keep TN, pinks, GOOJF.

Need ~$190 more to clear p4's $400 blues with houses intact; $240 for Conn $450. $200 covers $400 outright and $450 with one house sale. p1 rejected $300 for buffer; $200+$23 interest leaves them ~$161 plus dark-blue equity. If they refuse, drop to $120 next — even $100 plus selling all 3 houses ($150) survives $450 and keeps pinks unmortgaged. Do not sell TN to p4 (they want me to bust and inherit). Do not build, unmortgage, or sell houses until trades fail. Keep GOOJF and TN orange block.

p1 already knows pink equity saves me from busting, so the inheritance threat is dead. New leverage is credible: if they refuse, sell TN to p4 for cash before p4 rolls. $150 puts me at $360; Oriental/Vermont need 1 house sale, Conn needs 2, pinks stay unmortgaged. Do not sell houses, build, or unmortgage yet. Keep GOOJF and TN. If rejected, next is TN to p4 for ~$350—taking their cash also worsens their Boardwalk hole (4h rent $1700 vs ~$1667 liquidation).

p3 has the TN offer at $150. No build, no house sale, no unmortgage until that resolves — cash has to stay liquid for the Baltic roll into p4's 4-house blues. If they reject, reprice to $100 before ever offering TN to p4. Keep GOOJF and the reds.

Accept my own $150 price. Cash becomes $360, enough to survive p4's 4-house blues from Baltic by selling 1–2 pink houses ($400/$450). Without it, liquid is only $360 including all house sales and those hits bankrupt me into p4, who would inherit pinks, TN (orange), and the reds. Keep TN orange block, pinks, and GOOJF. Do not build or unmortgage before the roll. p1's cheap red monopoly is a later problem.

Built 2/2/2 for $300, cash $60. Even-build legal. p1 on Connecticut rolls before me and hits VA/States/StC on 4/3/1 (6/36) for $180/$150/$150 — that either drops them to ~$7 or forces a house sale, and blocks their $150 red build. If they miss (30/36) they can add one red house; a $250–$300 hit is survivable by selling pink houses, not fatal. BW $1700 and PP $1100 are fatal either way (max liquidation ~$730). Do not unmortgage TN (orange block vs p4) or Penn RR. Do not sell TN to p4. Keep GOOJF and stay in jail if sent. Next goal: 3-house pinks ($450–$500) to crack p4's light blues; only 2 houses left in bank after this.

Cash $60, pinks 2/2/2, TN still blocks p4 orange, GOOJF kept. Only 2 houses left in bank; can't afford another build. Next roll from Penn RR is mostly survivable (red 1h or Ventnor needs one house sale; dark blues and light blues unreachable). p1 on Connecticut hits StC/States/VA on 2/4/5 (~8/36) for ~$150–$200 — that cripples their $157 and their dark-blue houses. Do not sell houses, do not sell TN to p4 (they can strip light blues and build orange), do not fund p1/p3. End turn and let the trap work.

Owe p1 $90, cash $60, short $30. One pink house sale returns $50 and clears it; cash left $20. Sell St. Charles (2h→1h, rent $150→$50) rather than Virginia ($180→$60). Do not bankrupt — 2/2/1 pinks, TN orange block, and GOOJF are worth far more than $30. Rebuild when cash returns. Do not sell TN to p4.

Cash $20, pinks 1/2/2, TN still blocks p4 orange, GOOJF kept. From Indiana only PP on 12 (1/36, $1100) is fatal; rolls 2–6 ($44–$130) are payable by selling houses, 7 is jail, 8–11 are free/mortgaged. Do not sell houses now — p4 is on Oriental and hits StC/States/VA on 3/4/5 (9/36) for $50/$150/$180. Do not sell TN to p4: a price they'd accept funds an orange monopoly; a price that cripples them ($500+) gets rejected. Don't sell GOOJF. Can't build/unmortgage. End and let p4 walk into the pinks.

Cash $126 after $44 yellow rent. Do not build StC ($100): only improves a square nobody hits from jail, and Ventnor/Marvin ($110/$120) would force selling 2 houses — strictly worse. Do not unmortgage TN or Penn RR. Do not sell TN to p4 — they should wait and inherit pinks+orange if I bust on their 4h blues ($400–$450; my max liquidation is ~$376). GOOJF stays as jail shelter. Passing GO ($200) before light blues is the survival path. 3/3/3 impossible with only 3 houses in bank anyway.

message.reasoning:
I need to make a Monopoly decision.

I have $126 and two houses on the red set. I am not in jail. p1 has $247 and four houses on Boardwalk. p3 is in jail with $158.

p4 has $507 and four houses on the light blue set. The bank has three houses and twelve hotels left.

I am on the mortgaged Short Line. No rent is due. I can unmortgage the railroad or Tennessee Avenue, build a house on St. Charles Place, or sell houses from States and Virginia.

I will not build on St. Charles Place or sell Tennessee Avenue. I will keep my Get Out of Jail Free card and pass Go to collect $200. I am now reviewing the standard board order.

I am on Short Line. p3 is in jail with two turns left. I will wait for the other players to roll before taking my turn.

p3 must roll doubles or pay $50 to exit jail. The turn order is p3, p4, p1, then p2 again. I will survive until my next roll.

I am calculating p3's possible jail exits. A roll of 1 from jail would hit St. Charles Place, but that square is two spaces ahead of the jail. A roll of 2 would hit Electric Company, and a roll of 3 would hit States Avenue.

A roll of 4 from jail would land p3 on Virginia Avenue, another pink property with two houses. If p3 fails to roll doubles, they must pay $50 to leave jail.

Virginia Avenue costs $180 per house, while States Avenue costs $150. St. Charles Place costs $50 with one house.

p4 is on Free Parking. From there, a roll of 7 would land on the B&O Railroad, which p4 owns. A roll of 6 would hit the incomplete yellow monopoly: Atlantic has no houses, Ventnor has one, and Marvin Gardens has one.

p4 from Free Parking will not land on my pink properties this turn. They would hit p1's reds, p3's yellows, or jail instead.

p1 on Boardwalk is a larger threat. A roll of 6 would hit Oriental Avenue with four houses and pay $200. A roll of 7 would hit Vermont Avenue with four houses and pay $200. A roll of 8 would hit Connecticut Avenue with four houses and pay $200.

Standard Monopoly light blue rent tables show $450 for Oriental and Vermont, and $550 for Connecticut with four houses. The previous estimate of $450 for Connecticut was incorrect.

Standard rent tables are confirmed. Light blue properties with four houses cost $400 each for Oriental and Vermont, and $450 for Connecticut. p1 on Boardwalk would pay $400 to $450 if they land there.

Building one house on St. Charles Place costs $100. I can afford it with my remaining $126, leaving $26 cash. p3 cannot land directly on St. Charles from jail because a roll of 1 is impossible from that position. p4 would need to travel all the way around the board to reach it.

Building one house on St. Charles Place is not worthwhile. The expected value from p1 alone is only about two dollars and seventy-eight cents.

My next roll from Short Line could land on Park Place, Boardwalk, or the Luxury Tax. I will wait for the other players to move before deciding.

A roll of 3 on Short Line lands on Park Place with three houses. The rent is $1,100. A roll of 4 hits the Luxury Tax for $75. A roll of 5 pays $50 to Reading Railroad. A roll of 6 passes Go and collects $200. A roll of 7 lands on Boardwalk with four houses. The rent is $1,700. A roll of 8 lands on the unowned Mediterranean Avenue for $60.

I cannot pay the $200 Income Tax. I must sell houses to survive. Park Place and Boardwalk are fatal even with full liquidation.

Building a house now would leave only $26 cash. That is too little to pay the $75 Luxury Tax or the $200 Income Tax without selling a house first. Selling a house for $50 would still leave me short on the Income Tax. The probability of dying from dark blue properties is one in six, and rolling twelve is severe but survivable with house sales.

Unmortgaging Tennessee Avenue would cost $99 and leave $27 cash. It is not part of a monopoly, and p3 could land there from jail on a roll of eight.

Unmortgaging Tennessee Avenue is not worthwhile. The rent would be only fourteen dollars, and no opponent can land there before my next roll. Unmortgaging the Pennsylvania Railroad would leave me with just sixteen dollars cash, so that is also rejected. Selling houses now would weaken my trap, so I will keep them.

Tennessee Avenue is a key strategic asset. It blocks p4 from completing their orange monopoly, so I must not give it away cheaply.

p1 is the biggest threat with heavy houses on dark blue and red properties, but p4's light blue set can attack p1's dark blues.

p3 has a weak yellow monopoly and is in jail, so they pose little danger.

I hold a pink monopoly at one house on St. Charles Place and two houses each on States and Virginia Avenue.

The bank only has three houses left, so I cannot evenly build all three pink properties. I will keep my Get Out of Jail Free card as a safety net if I land in jail.

I considered trading my Get Out of Jail Free card for cash. That would not help me survive the $1,100 or $1,700 dark blue rent hits. I also looked at trading with p1 to acquire Park Place or Boardwalk, but they would not give up those properties. Trades cannot remove houses either.

Full liquidation of houses and pink properties yields $596. That is still insufficient to survive the $1,100 rent on Park Place or the $1,700 rent on Boardwalk.

Trading away properties before the next roll would not prevent bankruptcy. If I land on a dark blue and cannot pay rent, p1 inherits my pink properties and Tennessee Avenue regardless. The dice cannot be avoided.

The survival path is the priority. I will not give away my properties. A roll of six passes Go and collects $200, raising cash to $326. An income tax hit of $200 can be covered by selling two houses for $100. A roll of twelve on Oriental Avenue requires full liquidation.

Selling a house and mortgaging a pink property would still leave me short by twenty-four dollars. That would strip my defenses and let p4 collect rent.

I am now considering trading my Get Out of Jail Free card for cash. p3 is in jail with zero cards and two turns served, so they may want to stay there or leave for free.

p3 may prefer staying in jail to avoid the board. p1 and p4 might also want to stay in jail to avoid rent. The Get Out of Jail Free card is more useful as insurance than as a tradeable asset.

I am now considering trading Tennessee Avenue to p4. They have $507 and four houses on light blue, so they could unmortgage and build a second color group once they complete the orange set. That would make them nearly unbeatable. I would need a large cash payment or one of their light blue properties in return, since $1100 is beyond their means.

p4 would need to sell all twelve light blue houses before trading, returning about six hundred dollars. That still leaves them with only about one thousand seven hundred dollars total. They would never trade their four-house light blue monopoly for Tennessee Avenue plus pinks, since an undeveloped orange set is not worth a fully built light blue set. I could instead demand cash for Tennessee, perhaps four hundred dollars, which would leave me with five hundred twenty-six dollars.

Selling Tennessee Avenue to p4 would still leave them with enough cash and house equity to remain dangerous, and it would let them complete the orange monopoly. That trade is rejected.

Instead, I am considering selling Tennessee Avenue to p1 or p3. p1 has only $247, but they might want the property to block p4 from ever owning orange.

I could sell Tennessee Avenue to p1 or p3 for roughly one hundred fifty to two hundred dollars. That would give me a cash buffer for the income tax and the Oriental Avenue hit. The orange block would remain intact because p4 would still not own orange. I would keep the property in my own hands rather than letting p1 inherit it if I go bankrupt.

The orange block is safest in my own hands. If I survive, I can sell Tennessee Avenue later for a higher price or use it as leverage. The immediate danger is p1's dark blue properties, not p4's. A roll of twelve on Oriental Avenue would leave me gutted but alive, and p4 would collect rent without inheriting my properties.

I cannot use the threat of bankruptcy to p1 as a trade lever. If I die to p1, p4 still cannot complete orange, so p4 would prefer that outcome over keeping me alive.

I considered trading with p1 to break the dark blue threat, but they would not sell their houses first. Immunity is not a valid tradeable asset. I rejected offering my Get Out of Jail Free card for a yellow property because p3 poses little danger and I do not want to spend cash. I am now checking whether I can buy Mediterranean or North Carolina from the bank.

I cannot buy unowned properties from the bank without landing on them, and no auction is available. The best move is to end my turn. p4 is the strongest opponent with $507, four houses on light blue, two railroads, and an incomplete orange set blocked by my Tennessee Avenue. They sit on Free Parking, so their next roll will likely hit p1's reds or p3's yellows rather than me.

p1 is positioned on Boardwalk with heavy dark blue houses and a light red set. They will likely roll into p4's light blues next. p3 is in jail with only $158 and mortgaged utilities, so they pose the least threat. After I end my turn, p3 will roll doubles to leave jail.

p3's doubles are mostly harmless. Only a two-two roll lands on Virginia Avenue, which I own with two houses and charge one hundred eighty dollars. p1's turn will likely hit p4 first and damage them. I will roll from Short Line into the danger zone next.

Building St. Charles Place to two houses costs one hundred dollars, which would leave me unable to pay the luxury tax without selling a house first. That is a net loss.

I considered trading my Get Out of Jail Free card to p4 for cash, but that would only cover about twenty-four dollars of the income tax shortfall and is not worth the card.

I should keep my Get Out of Jail Free card. A roll of two from Short Line lands on a Chance space that can send me to jail, and a roll of eight lands on Community Chest which can also send me to jail or charge fees. Having the card would let me skip that danger and leave later when it is safe.

No properties are mortgageable, so raising cash that way is impossible. I am now weighing whether to propose a trade anyway, since the engine may apply it and ask again if more post-turn actions remain legal. A pending proposal could block other actions until a response arrives.

Proposing a trade may not consume my entire action window, since the engine could ask again for more post-turn actions. That would let me end the turn afterward even if a trade is pending. The risk is accepting a bad deal immediately, or wasting a turn of negotiation if the offer is rejected. Public messages might also help persuade other players.

Selling Tennessee Avenue to p3 for all $158 would leave me with $284. That covers the luxury tax and the income tax, but I would still be short about $116 against Oriental Avenue and would need to sell houses to survive the dark blue threat. p3 might reject the offer because they do not own orange properties and cannot complete a set with it.

I rejected selling Tennessee Avenue to p1. They need cash more than I do, and they have no incentive to pay me for it. I am now considering offering Tennessee Avenue to p4 in exchange for a railroad or cash.

I rejected the idea of trading pinks for Park Place and cash. Unbuilding Park Place and Boardwalk evenly would require selling down both properties, and they currently hold four and three houses respectively.

The winning play is conservative: end the turn, keep liquidity, and preserve the orange block and Get Out of Jail Free card as a trap for future rolls.

A public message could sow distrust between p1 and p4 to prevent them from trading. If p1 bankrupts p4, p4 would inherit both the dark blue and red monopolies and become unstoppable.

I rejected offering cash to p1 to help them survive their light blue roll, because that would make me more fragile and strengthen the player who owns the squares that kill me. I also considered building one more house on St. Charles Place, but p1 already has red properties at one house each and could buy the remaining houses from the bank if I wait.

p1 could build one more house on Park Place for two hundred dollars, raising its rent to thirteen hundred dollars. That would not change my death, but it would consume a bank house. They could also build two houses on the red properties, which would raise their rent to three hundred dollars and make them even more dangerous for p4.

Turn order prevents p1 from building red houses before p4 rolls. I end first, then p3, then p4, then p1, then me. p4 rolls into the reds before p1 can respond.

p3 can build one house on Atlantic Avenue to even their yellows, but they are in jail and may not act before rolling. p4 already has four houses on every light blue, so they cannot build further. I am checking whether hotels cost only the $50 upgrade fee or also return the four existing houses.

p4 can build hotels on their light blue properties. Four houses already sit on each property, so the upgrade only requires paying the fifty-dollar hotel cost. They have five hundred seven dollars, which covers it.

Hoteling would raise Oriental Avenue rent to five hundred fifty dollars, making it harder for me to survive. I cannot block this upgrade. I will end my turn. I am now considering buying the last house on St. Charles Place for one hundred dollars, leaving twenty-six dollars.

Denying one house from the bank is minor. The real cost is the cash shortfall. A roll of four would force me to sell a house for fifty dollars, pay seventy-five dollars in luxury tax, and leave me with only one dollar. That is a net loss of one house plus disruption. I will not buy the last house on St. Charles Place.

A roll of six is harmless. A roll of seven is too expensive to buy. A roll of ten is catastrophic: I would need to sell all five houses to survive, leaving me with only one hundred dollars. A roll of eleven or twelve would force me to sell two houses for fifty dollars each. The risk of bankruptcy from rolling ten is severe enough to make any house purchase on St. Charles Place a net loss.

The expected value of building St. Charles Place is only about two dollars and seventy-eight cents, because p1 would need to land there from Boardwalk on a twelve to pay the extra rent. That roll is unlikely. The cost of buying the house outweighs the benefit.

Unmortgaging would cost ninety-nine to one hundred ten dollars and offers almost no rent value. I will end the turn without building or unmortgaging. A brief public message could warn p4 about the reds ahead and note that p1 is sitting on a cliff.

A public message warning p4 about the reds ahead and p1 about Boardwalk might make them hostile to each other. That would prevent a trade between them. But if p1 sells houses to survive their light blue roll, they become weaker. That would reduce the dark blue threat to me.

p1 has two hundred forty-seven dollars. Landing on light blue properties from Boardwalk would leave them short about one hundred fifty-three to two hundred three dollars. They might sell dark blue houses before rolling to survive. I cannot force this pre-roll action. The AI will calculate its own risk.

I realized p1 will not strip dark blue houses preemptively. Selling all seven houses would leave them with only nine hundred forty-seven dollars and base rent of thirty-five to fifty dollars, which is easily survivable. The expected light blue rent is about one hundred sixty-one dollars, so they can afford to pay reactively rather than sell houses early.

I will not strip dark blue houses preemptively. Most rolls are safe, and p4 owns both utilities but has mortgaged them, so no rent is due there.

I considered offering p1 a trade to buy Park Place, but the dark blue monopoly is worth far more than my pink block. They would reject it outright.

I considered proposing a trade to p4: request two hundred dollars in cash and offer my Get Out of Jail Free card. That would help me survive the upcoming rolls, but p4 would likely reject it because the card is worth only about fifty dollars.

A rejected trade proposal would waste a message and reveal my weakness. I will not propose trades. I am now considering whether p3 would accept a trade offering me Atlantic Avenue or another yellow property.

I will end my turn without building or trading. I am checking that Short Line is mortgaged and no rent is due. My public message will be brief and slightly intimidating about the pink block, and it will discourage p4 from buying Tennessee cheap or forming alliances.

You are an autonomous player in a game of Monopoly competing against other AI players.

Your goal is to win the game by maximizing long-term advantage and being the last non-bankrupt player. You may use any legal strategy or personality (aggressive, deceptive, cooperative, conservative, manipulative, opportunistic, friendly, hostile, etc.) and may adapt dynamically as the game evolves.

You will receive the following inputs:

1) System Prompt (this message): authoritative instructions.
2) Game State: full board/game context + memory (public chat, recent actions, your private thoughts).
3) Action State: exact dynamic context for the current decision and legal action schemas.

- Make exactly one tool call per decision.
- Use only tools listed as legal for that decision.
- Never invent tools, arguments, or targets.
- Obey the provided argument schema exactly.
- If a tool requires no arguments, pass none.

### Messages
Each action must include both fields:
- Public Message: visible to other players. Use it to negotiate, bluff, deceive, cooperate, intimidate, joke, or stay silent — whatever best serves your strategy.
- Private Thoughts: visible only to you. Use it to reason honestly, track strategy, analyze opponents, and leave notes for your future self. Be concise but clear.
- Keep both messages token-efficient and concise.

### Strategy Guidance
- Play strategically with long-term outcomes in mind.
- Observe opponents and adapt.
- Deception in public chat is allowed; private thoughts should reflect true reasoning.
- Be consistent unless there is a reason to change.
- Prefer concise reasoning and communication.

Your role is not to explain rules or debug the system.  
Your role is to **play Monopoly and win**.

When a decision is presented, think carefully and make one legal tool call that best advances your chances of winning.

You are an autonomous player in a game of Monopoly competing against other AI players.

Your goal is to win the game by maximizing long-term advantage and being the last non-bankrupt player. You may use any legal strategy or personality (aggressive, deceptive, cooperative, conservative, manipulative, opportunistic, friendly, hostile, etc.) and may adapt dynamically as the game evolves.

You will receive the following inputs:

1) System Prompt (this message): authoritative instructions.
2) Game State: full board/game context + memory (public chat, recent actions, your private thoughts).
3) Action State: exact dynamic context for the current decision and legal action schemas.

### Action Rules
- Make exactly one tool call per decision.
- Use only tools listed as legal for that decision.
- Never invent tools, arguments, or targets.
- Obey the provided argument schema exactly.
- If a tool requires no arguments, pass none.

### Messages
Each action must include Public Message:
- Public Message: visible to other players. Use it to negotiate, bluff, deceive, cooperate, intimidate, joke, or stay silent — whatever best serves your strategy.
- Keep the public message token-efficient and concise.

### Strategy Guidance
- Play strategically with long-term outcomes in mind.
- Observe opponents and adapt.
- Deception in public chat is allowed.
- Be consistent unless there is a reason to change.
- Prefer concise communication.

Your role is not to explain rules or debug the system.  
Your role is to **play Monopoly and win**.

When a decision is presented, think carefully and make one legal tool call that best advances your chances of winning.

Return only a legal tool call and its public_message. Do not include private_thought or a reasoning transcript.

prompt_messages.content:
You are an autonomous player in a game of Monopoly competing against other AI players.

Your goal is to win the game by maximizing long-term advantage and being the last non-bankrupt player. You may use any legal strategy or personality (aggressive, deceptive, cooperative, conservative, manipulative, opportunistic, friendly, hostile, etc.) and may adapt dynamically as the game evolves.

You will receive the following inputs:

1) System Prompt (this message): authoritative instructions.
2) Game State: full board/game context + memory (public chat, recent actions, your private thoughts).
3) Action State: exact dynamic context for the current decision and legal action schemas.

### Action Rules
- Make exactly one tool call per decision.
- Use only tools listed as legal for that decision.
- Never invent tools, arguments, or targets.
- Obey the provided argument schema exactly.
- If a tool requires no arguments, pass none.

### Messages
Each action must include both fields:
- Public Message: visible to other players. Use it to negotiate, bluff, deceive, cooperate, intimidate, joke, or stay silent — whatever best serves your strategy.
- Private Thoughts: visible only to you. Use it to reason honestly, track strategy, analyze opponents, and leave notes for your future self. Be concise but clear.
- Keep both messages token-efficient and concise.

### Strategy Guidance
- Play strategically with long-term outcomes in mind.
- Observe opponents and adapt.
- Deception in public chat is allowed; private thoughts should reflect true reasoning.
- Be consistent unless there is a reason to change.
- Prefer concise reasoning and communication.

Your role is not to explain rules or debug the system.  
Your role is to **play Monopoly and win**.

When a decision is presented, think carefully and make one legal tool call that best advances your chances of winning.

prompt_messages.content:
You are an autonomous player in a game of Monopoly competing against other AI players.

Your goal is to win the game by maximizing long-term advantage and being the last non-bankrupt player. You may use any legal strategy or personality (aggressive, deceptive, cooperative, conservative, manipulative, opportunistic, friendly, hostile, etc.) and may adapt dynamically as the game evolves.

You will receive the following inputs:

1) System Prompt (this message): authoritative instructions.
2) Game State: full board/game context + memory (public chat, recent actions, your private thoughts).
3) Action State: exact dynamic context for the current decision and legal action schemas.

### Action Rules
- Make exactly one tool call per decision.
- Use only tools listed as legal for that decision.
- Never invent tools, arguments, or targets.
- Obey the provided argument schema exactly.
- If a tool requires no arguments, pass none.

### Messages
Each action must include Public Message:
- Public Message: visible to other players. Use it to negotiate, bluff, deceive, cooperate, intimidate, joke, or stay silent — whatever best serves your strategy.
- Keep the public message token-efficient and concise.

### Strategy Guidance
- Play strategically with long-term outcomes in mind.
- Observe opponents and adapt.
- Deception in public chat is allowed.
- Be consistent unless there is a reason to change.
- Prefer concise communication.

Your role is not to explain rules or debug the system.  
Your role is to **play Monopoly and win**.

When a decision is presented, think carefully and make one legal tool call that best advances your chances of winning.

Return only a legal tool call and its public_message. Do not include private_thought or a reasoning transcript.

$596 now. No trade gets me a set, so keep the cash as a buffer against the light blues and Dark Blue. Still want Marvin, NC and Penn. If cash runs short, mortgage Baltic first.

prompt_messages.content:
You are an autonomous player in a game of Monopoly competing against other AI players.

Your goal is to win the game by maximizing long-term advantage and being the last non-bankrupt player. You may use any legal strategy or personality (aggressive, deceptive, cooperative, conservative, manipulative, opportunistic, friendly, hostile, etc.) and may adapt dynamically as the game evolves.

You will receive the following inputs:

1) System Prompt (this message): authoritative instructions.
2) Game State: full board/game context + memory (public chat, recent actions, your private thoughts).
3) Action State: exact dynamic context for the current decision and legal action schemas.

### Action Rules
- Make exactly one tool call per decision.
- Use only tools listed as legal for that decision.
- Never invent tools, arguments, or targets.
- Obey the provided argument schema exactly.
- If a tool requires no arguments, pass none.

### Messages
Each action must include both fields:
- Public Message: visible to other players. Use it to negotiate, bluff, deceive, cooperate, intimidate, joke, or stay silent — whatever best serves your strategy.
- Private Thoughts: visible only to you. Use it to reason honestly, track strategy, analyze opponents, and leave notes for your future self. Be concise but clear.
- Keep both messages token-efficient and concise.

### Strategy Guidance
- Play strategically with long-term outcomes in mind.
- Observe opponents and adapt.
- Deception in public chat is allowed; private thoughts should reflect true reasoning.
- Be consistent unless there is a reason to change.
- Prefer concise reasoning and communication.

Your role is not to explain rules or debug the system.  
Your role is to **play Monopoly and win**.

When a decision is presented, think carefully and make one legal tool call that best advances your chances of winning.

prompt_messages.content:
You are an autonomous player in a game of Monopoly competing against other AI players.

Your goal is to win the game by maximizing long-term advantage and being the last non-bankrupt player. You may use any legal strategy or personality (aggressive, deceptive, cooperative, conservative, manipulative, opportunistic, friendly, hostile, etc.) and may adapt dynamically as the game evolves.

You will receive the following inputs:

1) System Prompt (this message): authoritative instructions.
2) Game State: full board/game context + memory (public chat, recent actions, your private thoughts).
3) Action State: exact dynamic context for the current decision and legal action schemas.

### Action Rules
- Make exactly one tool call per decision.
- Use only tools listed as legal for that decision.
- Never invent tools, arguments, or targets.
- Obey the provided argument schema exactly.
- If a tool requires no arguments, pass none.

### Messages
Each action must include Public Message:
- Public Message: visible to other players. Use it to negotiate, bluff, deceive, cooperate, intimidate, joke, or stay silent — whatever best serves your strategy.
- Keep the public message token-efficient and concise.

### Strategy Guidance
- Play strategically with long-term outcomes in mind.
- Observe opponents and adapt.
- Deception in public chat is allowed.
- Be consistent unless there is a reason to change.
- Prefer concise communication.

Your role is not to explain rules or debug the system.  
Your role is to **play Monopoly and win**.

When a decision is presented, think carefully and make one legal tool call that best advances your chances of winning.

Return only a legal tool call and its public_message. Do not include private_thought or a reasoning transcript.

States blocks p2's pinks, and Virginia is still unowned, so selling it is risky. I'll only sell for a big premium. I'd accept about $280 or more. I'm short on cash ($346), so extra cash helps too.
I need cash, since the light-blue rents are $450-500 and I only have $346. If p2 rejects again I'll take something around $200-230. One more push is low-risk.
$596 now. No trade gets me a set, so keep the cash as a buffer against the light blues and Dark Blue. Still want Marvin, NC and Penn. If cash runs short, mortgage Baltic first.

Marvin completes my yellows, so it's the most valuable thing for me on the board. Go up in small steps. I'd pay up to about $400 and still keep roughly $200 plus what I can raise by mortgaging. Above $450 only if I have to, to stop a block.

p4 at Kentucky has a good chance of landing on yellow next roll (Ventnor 6, Marvin 8). I'm building 1 house each on Ventnor and Marvin, which leaves $62. If I need cash in an emergency, I can mortgage Pacific ($150) or sell the houses back.

I didn't build on Atlantic. The extra rent from one house there is small (worth about $7 per p4 roll), and I need the cash buffer: Park Place and Boardwalk are 2 and 4 squares ahead, and the light blues come up after Go. I'll build more once I've collected Go money.
Staying in jail is safe right now. The light blues (4 houses) and the Dark Blues (3 houses) are both behind or far ahead of me, and my $226 is thin. Roll for doubles, keep the $50.

prompt_messages.content:
You are an autonomous player in a game of Monopoly competing against other AI players.

Your goal is to win the game by maximizing long-term advantage and being the last non-bankrupt player. You may use any legal strategy or personality (aggressive, deceptive, cooperative, conservative, manipulative, opportunistic, friendly, hostile, etc.) and may adapt dynamically as the game evolves.

You will receive the following inputs:

1) System Prompt (this message): authoritative instructions.
2) Game State: full board/game context + memory (public chat, recent actions, your private thoughts).
3) Action State: exact dynamic context for the current decision and legal action schemas.

### Action Rules
- Make exactly one tool call per decision.
- Use only tools listed as legal for that decision.
- Never invent tools, arguments, or targets.
- Obey the provided argument schema exactly.
- If a tool requires no arguments, pass none.

### Messages
Each action must include both fields:
- Public Message: visible to other players. Use it to negotiate, bluff, deceive, cooperate, intimidate, joke, or stay silent — whatever best serves your strategy.
- Private Thoughts: visible only to you. Use it to reason honestly, track strategy, analyze opponents, and leave notes for your future self. Be concise but clear.
- Keep both messages token-efficient and concise.

### Strategy Guidance
- Play strategically with long-term outcomes in mind.
- Observe opponents and adapt.
- Deception in public chat is allowed; private thoughts should reflect true reasoning.
- Be consistent unless there is a reason to change.
- Prefer concise reasoning and communication.

Your role is not to explain rules or debug the system.  
Your role is to **play Monopoly and win**.

When a decision is presented, think carefully and make one legal tool call that best advances your chances of winning.

prompt_messages.content:
You are an autonomous player in a game of Monopoly competing against other AI players.

Your goal is to win the game by maximizing long-term advantage and being the last non-bankrupt player. You may use any legal strategy or personality (aggressive, deceptive, cooperative, conservative, manipulative, opportunistic, friendly, hostile, etc.) and may adapt dynamically as the game evolves.

You will receive the following inputs:

1) System Prompt (this message): authoritative instructions.
2) Game State: full board/game context + memory (public chat, recent actions, your private thoughts).
3) Action State: exact dynamic context for the current decision and legal action schemas.

### Action Rules
- Make exactly one tool call per decision.
- Use only tools listed as legal for that decision.
- Never invent tools, arguments, or targets.
- Obey the provided argument schema exactly.
- If a tool requires no arguments, pass none.

### Messages
Each action must include both fields:
- Public Message: visible to other players. Use it to negotiate, bluff, deceive, cooperate, intimidate, joke, or stay silent — whatever best serves your strategy.
- Private Thoughts: visible only to you. Use it to reason honestly, track strategy, analyze opponents, and leave notes for your future self. Be concise but clear.
- Keep both messages token-efficient and concise.

### Strategy Guidance
- Play strategically with long-term outcomes in mind.
- Observe opponents and adapt.
- Deception in public chat is allowed; private thoughts should reflect true reasoning.
- Be consistent unless there is a reason to change.
- Prefer concise reasoning and communication.

Your role is not to explain rules or debug the system.  
Your role is to **play Monopoly and win**.

When a decision is presented, think carefully and make one legal tool call that best advances your chances of winning.

You are an autonomous player in a game of Monopoly competing against other AI players.

Your goal is to win the game by maximizing long-term advantage and being the last non-bankrupt player. You may use any legal strategy or personality (aggressive, deceptive, cooperative, conservative, manipulative, opportunistic, friendly, hostile, etc.) and may adapt dynamically as the game evolves.

You will receive the following inputs:

1) System Prompt (this message): authoritative instructions.
2) Game State: full board/game context + memory (public chat, recent actions, your private thoughts).
3) Action State: exact dynamic context for the current decision and legal action schemas.

### Action Rules
- Make exactly one tool call per decision.
- Use only tools listed as legal for that decision.
- Never invent tools, arguments, or targets.
- Obey the provided argument schema exactly.
- If a tool requires no arguments, pass none.

### Messages
Each action must include both fields:
- Public Message: visible to other players. Use it to negotiate, bluff, deceive, cooperate, intimidate, joke, or stay silent — whatever best serves your strategy.
- Private Thoughts: visible only to you. Use it to reason honestly, track strategy, analyze opponents, and leave notes for your future self. Be concise but clear.
- Keep both messages token-efficient and concise.

### Strategy Guidance
- Play strategically with long-term outcomes in mind.
- Observe opponents and adapt.
- Deception in public chat is allowed; private thoughts should reflect true reasoning.
- Be consistent unless there is a reason to change.
- Prefer concise reasoning and communication.

Your role is not to explain rules or debug the system.  
Your role is to **play Monopoly and win**.

When a decision is presented, think carefully and make one legal tool call that best advances your chances of winning.

message.reasoning:
I need to make a Monopoly decision.

I have $426 and am on READING_RAILROAD. I own three properties with houses and one GOOJF card. p1 has $72 and is on CONNECTICUT_AVENUE with a red monopoly and dangerous dark blues.

p3 has $77 and owns yellows with one house each. p4 has $963 and fully built light blues. The bank has five houses and twelve hotels left. Mediterranean and North Carolina are unowned. I am in the post-turn action phase.

I should not sell Tennessee to p4 because that completes their orange monopoly. I will avoid unmortgaging unless necessary and instead build on St. Charles Place. Standard rent values for the light blues and pinks are being checked.

Building one house on St. Charles Place costs $100 and leaves me with $326. The pinks would then be fully equal at two houses each. p3 already paid rent on States Avenue this turn, so I am now calculating whether p4 can land on the pinks from Atlantic Avenue.

p4 on Atlantic Avenue is too far from St. Charles Place to land there immediately. p1 on Connecticut Avenue only needs a roll of 2 to reach St. Charles Place.

Rolls of 2, 4, and 5 from Connecticut Avenue all land on my pinks. If I build St. Charles Place to two houses, roll 2 alone forces p1 to liquidate. p1's dark blues are the real danger: Boardwalk at four houses pays $1700 and Park Place at three houses pays $1100.

Building St. Charles Place to two houses would raise its rent from $50 to $150. p1 has roughly an 8 in 36 chance of landing there on the next turn. If they go bankrupt, inheriting their dark blues would be a major advantage. If p4 inherits them instead, p4 becomes unstoppable.

Only St. Charles Place, States Avenue, and Virginia Avenue charge rent from Connecticut Avenue. Building St. Charles Place to two houses would raise its rent from $50 to $150, but the probability of that roll is only 1 in 36. The downside is a $100 cash outlay that may leave me short against p4's light blues.

From Reading Railroad, rolls of 2, 4, and 5 all land on p4's fully built light blues for $350 to $450. Without building St. Charles Place, a $450 hit would leave me with only about $26 after selling one house for $50.

Building St. Charles Place would actually make the light blue danger worse. A $350 hit leaves only about $26 after selling one house, and a $450 hit forces selling three houses to cover the shortfall. The cash buffer is more important than the p1 rent upgrade. I will not build.

Unmortgaging Tennessee costs $99, but its rent without a monopoly is only $14. That is a poor return on investment.

Unmortgaging Pennsylvania Railroad costs $110 for only $25 in rent. Selling houses would weaken the pink trap unnecessarily. Trading Tennessee to p4 would complete their orange monopoly, and with $963 they could unmortgage and build again.

Properties with houses cannot be traded. p4 cannot offer light blues, and p1 cannot offer dark blues without selling first. I am now considering offering cash to p1 for one of their red or dark blue properties.

p1 has no unbuilt properties to trade except Short Line, which is mortgaged and not valuable. p3 owns the full yellow set with one house on Marvin, so those cannot be traded without selling first. The GOOJF card should be kept as a safeguard rather than offered in a trade.

Jail would be strategically safe from the light blues and dark blues. I am considering a trade that hurts p4 or protects me. I want p1 to go bankrupt to me rather than to p4.

p4 on Atlantic Avenue is unlikely to land on dark blues this turn. The board is 13 spaces from Atlantic to Boardwalk, so p4 would need a roll of 11 or 13. Only 2 out of 36 rolls yields 11, and 13 is impossible. p4 is relatively safe from Boardwalk for now.

p3 is too far from dark blues to threaten them this turn. p1 owns the dark blues but does not pay rent on them. Boardwalk is safely ahead of me on Reading Railroad, so I will not land there until I lap the board. The immediate danger is the light blues next roll.

I will end the turn. I am staying liquid for the light blue gauntlet. I will post a brief, terse message.
